points.description: States that a function pointer is an address (a pointer/variable holding the address) of where the function's code is located in memory, in any wording.
points.partial_credit: 2-3 marks if it only says it is a pointer related to a function (e.g. points to or is used to call a function) without the idea of memory address/location of the function code.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a function pointer holds or is the memory address of a function (its code), however briefly or informally worded. Give part marks if the answer is on the right track, e.g. 'a pointer that points to a function' or 'used to call a function' without mentioning address or memory. Give little or no marks if the answer describes something unrelated, such as a pointer returned by a function. Extra correct detail, such as syntax or uses, is fine.
